question.problem: If ${e}^{-y/4}+6=14,$ then $y≈${{field-1}}, rounded to $3$ decimal places.
question.worked_solution:
First, we rearrange our equation into a form that is more convenient for logarithms, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{-y/4}+6 & =14 \\ {e}^{-y/4} & =14-6 \\ {e}^{-y/4} & =8\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we find the natural logarithm $(ln)$ of both sides of the equation and solve for $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{-y/4} & =8 \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{-y/4}) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(8) \\ -\frac{y}{4} & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(8) \\ y & =-4\operatorname{ln}⁡(8)\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluating the above expression using a calculator gives

$$
y≈-8.318
$$

rounded to $3$ decimal places.
